checks.message: Lightsail instances get a public IP by default — verify firewall rules are locked down
checks.context: Every Lightsail instance is publicly reachable from the internet. The default firewall allows SSH (22) and HTTP (80) from anywhere. Restrict SSH to your IP and close any ports your app doesn't need.

checks.message: Opening all ports to the internet
checks.context: Exposing every port on a public instance is an immediate compromise waiting to happen. Automated scanners will find open services within minutes. Only open the specific ports your application needs.

checks.message: Instance deletion destroys the disk unless you create a snapshot first
checks.context: Lightsail instance disks are deleted with the instance by default. Take a manual snapshot before deleting if you need to preserve data or be able to recreate the instance.

checks.message: Lightsail database set to publicly accessible
checks.context: A publicly accessible database is reachable from the entire internet. Automated scanners will find it and attempt brute-force logins. Databases should only be accessible from within your Lightsail VPC.

checks.message: Verify bucket access permissions are set to private
checks.context: Lightsail buckets can be set to public, which makes all objects readable by anyone. Unlike S3, there's no Block Public Access setting — you have to explicitly set the access level to private.

checks.message: Attach an SSL/TLS certificate and enable HTTPS
checks.context: Lightsail load balancers support free SSL certificates via ACM. Without HTTPS, all traffic between clients and your load balancer is in plaintext. Enable HTTPS and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

checks.message: Verify closing this port doesn't break SSH access or application connectivity
checks.context: Closing port 22 locks you out of SSH access. Closing application ports (80, 443, etc.) immediately stops serving traffic. Verify you have an alternative access path before closing.

checks.message: Store the private key securely — it's displayed only once and cannot be retrieved later
checks.context: The private key is returned in the API response and never stored by AWS. If lost, you cannot recover it and must create a new key pair. Store it in a secrets manager, not in plaintext files.

checks.message: The certificate requires DNS or email validation before it becomes active
checks.context: The TLS certificate is issued by ACM but requires domain validation. Traffic remains unencrypted until validation completes. Monitor the validation status and complete it promptly.

checks.message: Verify snapshot encryption and access controls match your data classification
checks.context: Database snapshots contain a full copy of your database. If the snapshot is shared or the access controls are permissive, all data in the database is exposed.

checks.message: Unpeering immediately cuts connectivity between Lightsail and your VPC resources
checks.context: Any Lightsail instances communicating with EC2, RDS, or other VPC resources will lose connectivity immediately. Verify no active traffic depends on this peering before removing.

checks.message: Verify the database is not being made publicly accessible
checks.context: Lightsail relational databases support a publicly-accessible setting. Enabling it exposes the database to the internet. Keep databases private and access them through Lightsail instances.

checks.message: Parameter changes may require a database reboot to take effect
checks.context: Some parameter changes are applied immediately while others require a reboot. Verify which parameters are pending reboot and schedule maintenance accordingly to avoid unexpected downtime.
